newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - $5.2 bln in sales plus data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - $5.2 bln in sales plus data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds late on Friday were from flat to 1/4 point higher, buoyed by stronger Treasuries, but next week will see another flood of new issues, estimated at $5.175 billion, which could hit prices.
A total of around $4.8 billion of bonds were sold this week, with most deals doing surprisingly well.
"I don't think they gave up as much yield this week at they thought they would have to," a trader said.

For example, the largest offering, New Jersey Transportation Trust Fund Authority's $713 million of bonds, drew both institutional and retail demand, with speculation one large mutual fund bought as much as $200 million.
The bonds were won by Merrill Lynch at 5.4826 percent.
However, while this week was fairly quiet in terms of economic reports, next week will see a host of data, culminating in the payrolls report, which this year often has prompted sharp reactions.
That factor, plus the inventories of this week's deals that dealers have yet to find homes for, could give next week's offerings a bumpier ride.
"We made it through this week without too much trouble. But next week, with all the economic numbers and new supply, will be a challenge," a trader said.
The intermediate sector accounts for most of the volume of this week's offerings that still lingers on dealers shelves, traders said.
While selling volume, which was particularly active this week, subsided, traders noted that several blocks of New York paper were on some of the bid wanted lists being circulated.
There was speculation the sellers probably were trying to make room for next week's offerings, though some traders regarded the offering of such bonds as coincidental.
The New York State Dormitory Authority next week is selling $775 million taxable bonds and nearly $600 million of tax-exempt bonds from the New York State Urban Development Corp.

In secondary trading on Friday, Denver, Colo., City and County Airport revenue refunding bonds, Series C, 5.50s due 2015 and MBIA insured were bid 5.88 percent, up 6 basis points from Thursday, when they were bid 5.82 net.
The December U.S Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade rose 13 ticks to 111, mainly due to relief that the durable goods data was not as bearish as it first appeared.
Although this key measure of the manufacturing sector rose 4.6 percent, most of the gain was due to a 17.5 percent surge in transportation orders.
The December municipal bond futures also firmed, up 12 ticks to 114-11/32. As a result, the MOB spread fell one basis point to positive 107 ticks.
